Graphormer style graph transformer

Source: R/graph-transformers.R
graph_transformer_model.Rd

Input projection plus centrality encoding (a learned embedding of each node's clipped degree, added to the features), num_layers graph_transformer_layer()s with shortest path attention bias, a final layer norm, and either a node level linear head or global pooling and an MLP head. Shortest path distances are computed in R for each batch, which costs \(O(\sum_g n_g (n_g + e_g))\) per forward pass.

Usage

graph_transformer_model(
  input_dim,
  hidden_dim = 64L,
  output_dim = 1L,
  num_layers = 2L,
  heads = 4L,
  max_dist = 5L,
  max_degree = 10L,
  dropout = 0.1,
  pool = "mean"
)

Arguments

input_dim

Node feature size.

hidden_dim

Model width.

output_dim

Output size.

num_layers

Transformer layers.

heads

Attention heads.

max_dist

Largest distinguished shortest path distance.

max_degree

Degrees above this share one embedding.

dropout

Dropout probability.

pool

NULL for node level output, or "mean", "sum", "max".

Value

An nn_module of class graph_transformer.

Details

The forward signature matches gnn_model(), so the model works with train_graph_model().

References

Ying et al. (2021) Do transformers really perform badly for graph representation? NeurIPS.
